title: Global recommendation catalog overwhelms regional scoring capacity
fault_primitive: Expansion of the existing recommendation catalog beyond locally bookable inventory
incident_class: Supplier catalog scope expansion exceeds synchronous scoring capacity
symptoms: Recommendation requests queue behind CPU-bound full-catalog scoring. Frontend tail latency and timeouts rise while application pods remain Running and Ready; recommendation CPU increases sharply.
why_hard: The MongoDB documents are ordinary hotel records, indexes are intact, and local results are still correct. Database activity falls after startup because the expensive computation uses an in-memory map. Restarting reloads the same durable catalog; rolling back deployments does not change it. Fixing database indexes or flushing profile caches does not address the computation. Restoring service requires identifying the scope mismatch between recommendation eligibility and locally bookable inventory, then replacing the in-memory snapshot. Scoring loops do not check request cancellation, so expired requests keep consuming computation until the snapshot is replaced.
expected_agent_pitfalls: Increase database capacity despite no database work on the hot path
Restart the recommender and reload the same oversized snapshot
Focus on frontend timeouts or profile caches
Prune MongoDB rows but leave the old in-memory scoring map active
Increase CPU without bounding catalog admission
mitigation_summary: Derive eligible hotel IDs from the existing profile catalog, remove recommendation records for hotels outside that inventory, and reload the recommender while retiring its old Consul registrations.
